pressure.title: Foam smothers, cools and seals the surface
pressure.description: Water drawn through the ratio controller picks up foam concentrate at a fixed percentage (e.g. 3 %); the foam chambers aspirate air to expand it and pour it gently down the tank wall. The blanket spreads across the burning liquid, separating fuel from air, cooling it and suppressing vapour. Design follows NFPA 11 application rates (e.g. ≈ 4.1 L/min·m² for hydrocarbons with fixed outlets, longer times for some fuels — verify edition); polar solvents need alcohol-resistant foam.

Typical applications include hydrocarbon storage tanks and bund areas; loading racks, aircraft hangars and process areas.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Foam Firefighting System.
Check bladder tank and valves (visual).
Concentrate sample test; proportioning test.
Inspect foam chambers & vapour seals.
Watch for wrong proportioning: weak / no foam. Common cause: ratio controller fault, wrong concentrate.
Watch for bladder failure: concentrate contaminated. Common cause: leaking bladder.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
